newsitem.title: CONGO: Fighting near Brazzaville airport despite truce.
newsitem.headline: Fighting near Brazzaville airport despite truce.

text.p: Mortar blasts and grenade explosions echoed around some areas near the Brazzaville airport early on Thursday despite a ceasefire called to end a week of fighting between forces of dissident Congolese militia leader Denis Sassou Nguesso and the army of President Pascal Lissouba.
The city saw a few hours of quiet after Lissouba ordered his troops to stop firing on Wednesday afternoon and Sassou Nguesso urged his supporters to observe the ceasefire.
But sporadic shooting broke out close to a French base at the airport overnight and by dawn fairly heavy grenade and mortar fire could be heard from some areas near the airport, witnesses said.
"There was some firing but it was the quietest night we have had here for several days," one French officer said.

Clashes erupted in Congo last week after government troops surrounded the home of the former Marxist military leader Sassou Nguesso in a crackdown on militias ahead of a July 27 presidential election.
